newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-ROMERO TAKES ITALIAN LEAD AFTER MAKING UP FOR PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ROMERO TAKES ITALIAN LEAD AFTER MAKING UP FOR PENALTY.

text.p: Argentina's Eduardo Romero overcame the disadvantage of a two-stroke penalty to take the second-round lead in the Italian Open golf tournament on Friday.

The 42-year-old Romero, who won the Italian title in 1994, had the penalty imposed in the first round when his playing partners reported that he had grounded his putter illegally on his line during a practice putt.
Romero made up the strokes and picked up another for good measure as he carded a three-under-par 69 to move seven-under-par on 137 and into a one-shot lead.
Englishmen Gordon Brand and Brian Davis were a stroke behind, while a quadruple-bogey eight on the eighth plummeted overnight leader Retief Goosen down the leaderboard to three under with a 73.
Welshman Ian Woosnam, who had lain a shot behind Goosen overnight, erred at the end of his round with two bogeys to go back to four under with a 73.

The previous day's events served to unsettle leader Romero but he then shrugged off the two penalty shots to pick up three birdies. In two rounds he has collected nine birdies without dropping any strokes other than his penalty.

"I was worried at the start that I might not be able to get the penalty out of my mind," said Romero. "I trusted my playing partner the day before, Carl Mason, who reported that I had touched the line of my putt, even though I couldn't remember doing it, so I just had to get on with things and try to forget it.

"When I did, I went back to playing the fantastic golf I'm now capable of since changing my swing with my teaching uncle Mario Romero, who's also helped me with my putting stroke. I'm hitting the ball very well when I can concentrate properly and maybe I can win now even with the penalty strokes."
Goosen crashed off the top of the leaderboard with a 75 after going four-over-par on the eighth, losing a ball and hitting a shot into a ditch.
